content:
incident-bot: PAGER — P1: OrchID Health (vpc-orchid-prod) reporting KV/prefix cache hit-rate collapse in us-west-2. High latency and error spike for tenant 'orchid-health'. Pager routed to oncall SRE Maya Chen.

Maya Chen: ack — I'm oncall and looking. @Tom Alvarez can you join? I'll pull KV metrics and check prefetch queues.

Tom Alvarez: joining. running `curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/kv?tenant=orchid-health | jq .` — hit_rate: 0.12, evictions_per_sec: 420, prefetch_backlog: 2400. patterns show many high-cardinality temp prefixes.

Lina Park: support here — customer reports 5-25s tail latencies and ~10% 5xx from our side. They're in production traffic for a rollout.

Henry O'Neill: quick mitigation plan: 1) disable prefetch for tenant, 2) reduce tenant cache quota, 3) route hot writes to fallback/dedicated pool. Can ops flip config quickly?

Maya Chen: applying quick toggle now: `PATCH /config/vpcs/vpc-orchid-prod/tenants/orchid-health { "kv_prefetch_enabled": false }` — executing.

eng-runtime: seeing correlated KV TTL storm. Onboarding job `orchid-sync` spiked and created many short-lived prefixes (uuid sharded). Write rate to prefix namespace increased 18x.

Tom Alvarez: running `redis-cli --scan --pattern "orchid:temp:*" | wc -l` -> ~1.2M keys. Suggest targeted delete of `orchid:temp:*` with throttled `DEL`/`UNLINK` to avoid I/O spike.

Alex Ruiz: I'll own customer comms. Lina, please prep message saying we applied temporary mitigations (prefetch disabled, quota reduced) and will monitor.

Lina Park: draft: "We're investigating increased latency for your VPC. We've disabled a caching prefetch and reduced tenant cache quota as a temporary mitigation. You should see improvements within 5-10 minutes. We'll update with root cause and next steps." Want to add anything, Alex?

Alex Ruiz: good. add ETA for next update in 30m and contact alias.

Maya Chen: mitigation applied: prefetch disabled + set-prefix-quota orchid-health 0.05 (5% of pool). Starting controlled SCAN/UNLINK of `orchid:temp:*` with rate limit 2000 keys/sec.

Tom Alvarez: initial results: hit_rate -> 0.62 within 8m, p95 latency down from 18s -> 2.6s, 5xx down to 1.2%. Evictions/sec dropping. :thumbsup:

Henry O'Neill: good. next steps: 1) add a tenant-level circuit-breaker for prefetch storms, 2) enforce write-rate caps for onboarding jobs, 3) add a blacklist for ephemeral prefixes at runtime. Assign owners?

Tom Alvarez: I'll own the blacklist PR and the `INC-2021` ticket. Creating checklist and postmortem.

eng-runtime: I'll push a runtime patch to respect `prefix_blacklist` and add fast-path eviction for known ephemeral patterns. Will open PR and link to INC-2021.

Maya Chen: handing over to next oncall: @Henry O'Neill — I'm going offline in 30m. Leaving notes in the incident ticket and linking dashboards.

Henry O'Neill: taking over. Monitoring dashboards look stable. Customer comms sent. Will keep watch for 1hr then move to postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated; severity=P1 -> WATCH. Please acknowledge. :white_check_mark: 

Maya Chen: acknowledged.

Tom Alvarez: acknowledged, will follow up with postmortem and remediation timeline.

Lina Park: acknowledged. Updated customer channel with mitigation note.

Alex Ruiz: ack — prepping follow-up email.

eng-runtime: ack — PR in progress.

-- action items (summary) --
- Tom Alvarez: create postmortem (INC-2021) and implement prefix blacklist.
- eng-runtime: runtime circuit-breaker for tenant prefetch + fast eviction.
- Support (Lina/Alex): improve onboarding docs and advise customers about ephemeral-key patterns.
- Ops: add runbook step to isolate tenant prefix and throttled UNLINK procedure.

Maya Chen: closing handoff notes. P1 mitigated but watch for regressions.

Henry O'Neill: I'll keep an eye and schedule the follow-up meeting.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging; keep updates in the ticket.
